articleTitle: Modeling the learner group formation problem in computer-supported collaborative learning using mathematical programming
publicationTitle: The 8th National and the 5th International Conference on e-Learning and e-Teaching (ICeLeT 2014)
abstract: One of the main challenges in Computer- Supported Collaborative Learning (CSCL) is group formation. Various approaches have been reported in the literature to tackle this problem, but none have offered an optimal solution. In this study a novel binary integer programming formulation was proposed to model the group formation problem and optimally assign each learner to the most appropriate group. In this contribution an online class of 32 learners was divided into two sections. The groups in the first section were formed by means of our suggested method. In the other section a modified version of K-Means clustering algorithm was used to assign participants to appropriate groups. Findings revealed that the suggested model was successful in optimally solving the problem in 8.27 seconds, on average. The results also disclosed that the proposed technique generated better outcomes in theory and in practice.

articleTitle: E-SoRS: A personalized and social recommender service for E-learning environments
publicationTitle: The 8th National and the 5th International Conference on e-Learning and e-Teaching (ICeLeT 2014)
abstract: Education is one of the main application areas in personalized systems. Personalization is especially important for Web-based education due to at least two general reasons. First, most web-based applications are to be used by a much wider variety of users in comparison to traditional environments and personalization helps system suit users. Second, such systems are learner centric and users are working with it individually. Contextualization is a common way to make systems personalized. Context-aware systems can detect user’s situation better as well as act more efficiently in response to their needs. In this paper, a personalized context-aware learning system has been proposed to enhance learning effectiveness. Learner’s knowledge level, his/her social relation, distance of each relation, and learning style are some important criteria of the implemented system. Applying this context-aware system in a graduate-level course results in educational improvement and learner satisfaction. Due to the flexibility and scalability of the proposed model, we believe that it could be beneficial to very large learning organizations.

articleTitle: Normalization of CALL and TPACK: Teachers' opportunities and challenges
publicationTitle: The 8th National and the 5th International Conference on e-Learning and e-Teaching (ICeLeT 2014)
abstract: The present study aims at investigating the effect of technology integration in general and normalization of CALL in particular on Iranian teachers' technological, pedagogical, and content knowledge (TPACK). It also examines teachers' main opportunities and challenges with normalization of CALL. In this regard, 16 teachers taught a course with the goal to integrate computer technology fully. The researcher implemented a TPACK questionnaire before and after the course and a semistructured interview after the course. Observations also helped the researcher to gain a complementary understanding of the process of CALL normalization and how teachers deal with their new roles. The results revealed that technology-related knowledge domains developed significantly. The results also showed that Iranian educational society is highly sensitive to instructional technology and its use in education.
